acceptOwnership().details: The new owner accepts the ownership transfer.

computeKey(bytes32,uint256,address,addre.details: Takes the shared six-word key layout; `token` must be `address(0)`.

create(bytes32,address,address,uint256).details: The value always comes from msg.sender. The refundAddress param controls      who can call refund — useful for coordinators/routers acting on behalf of a user.

params.claimAddress: Address authorized to redeem the locked coins
params.preimageHash: SHA-256 hash of the secret preimage
params.refundAddress: Address that can refund after timelock (does not have to be msg.sender)
params.timelock: Unix timestamp after which the refund address can reclaim the coins

create(bytes32,address,uint256).details: Convenience wrapper — uses msg.sender as the sender (refund address)

params.claimAddress: Address authorized to redeem the locked coins
params.preimageHash: SHA-256 hash of the secret preimage — an indexed event topic,                      not an identifier: swaps may share one, and `key` tells them apart
params.timelock: Unix timestamp after which the sender can reclaim the coins

isActive(bytes32,uint256,address,address.details: Takes the shared six-word key layout so batch readers work unchanged;      `token` must be `address(0)`.

owner().details: Returns the address of the current owner.

pendingOwner().details: Returns the address of the pending owner.

recoverExcess(address).details: Nothing here accepts a plain transfer, so the balance can only exceed      `lockedTotal` through a force-send (selfdestruct, coinbase, or a transfer to the      address before deployment). Only that difference is movable: the subtraction      floors at what every active swap is owed, so no call here can reduce the balance      below the amount its settlements will need.

recoverToken(address,address).details: No swap here ever holds a token — the locked asset is the native coin — so      the full balance of any token belongs to nobody and is movable. An ERC20      transfer into this contract cannot be refused, hence this escape hatch.

redeem(bytes32,uint256,address,uint256).details: Only the designated claimAddress can call this — msg.sender is used as      claimAddress in the key lookup. The coins are sent to msg.sender.

params.preimage: Secret whose SHA-256 hash matches the preimageHash used at creation
params.timelock: Timelock that was set at creation

redeemBySig(bytes32,uint256,address,uint.details: Anyone may submit this call, but the signature binds `caller` to `msg.sender`,      so only the address the claimant named can settle with it. The coins are paid      to that caller unconditionally: `destination`, `sweepToken`, `minAmountOut` and      `callsHash` are hashed into the signed message so the caller cannot alter them,      but this contract does not act on them. They are guarantees only when `caller`      is a contract that enforces them after receiving the coins (the coordinator).      A signature whose `caller` is an EOA hands the swap amount to that EOA.

params.callsHash: Hash of the calls array (bound to signature, enforced by `caller`, not here)
params.destination: Address where the caller intends to route funds after redeem (bound to signature, enforced by `caller`, not here)
params.minAmountOut: Minimum amount of sweepToken required (bound to signature, enforced by `caller`, not here)
params.preimage: Secret whose SHA-256 hash matches the preimageHash used at creation
params.sweepToken: Token the caller will sweep to destination (bound to signature, enforced by `caller`, not here)
params.timelock: Timelock that was set at creation

returns.claimAddress: The address recovered from the signature

refund(bytes32,uint256,address,uint256).details: Convenience wrapper — the coins are sent back to msg.sender

params.claimAddress: Claim address that was set at creation
params.preimageHash: The preimage hash used at creation
params.timelock: Timelock that was set at creation

refund(bytes32,uint256,address,uint256,a.details: msg.sender must still be the original sender (enforced via the hash).      Useful for sending the coins to a coordinator/router for further processing,      or for a sender that cannot itself receive the native coin.

params.claimAddress: Claim address that was set at creation
params.destination: Address to receive the refunded coins
params.preimageHash: The preimage hash used at creation
params.timelock: Timelock that was set at creation

refundBySig(bytes32,uint256,uint256,uint.details: Collaborative refund. Both parties consent — the sender by being msg.sender      (exactly as in `refund`), the claimAddress by an EIP-712 signature over the      swap terms with `sender = msg.sender`. The signature only waives the timelock;      it moves nothing on its own. A claimAddress that signs and then calls with      itself as sender addresses a key it never funded, so it cannot route the      locked coins to itself. The coins go to msg.sender.      No expiry on the signature, on purpose: it is bound to one key, and that key      can leave Active exactly once, so every signature over it dies with the first      settlement that lands.

params.preimageHash: The preimage hash used at creation (not the preimage — the                     sender does not know it)
params.timelock: Timelock that was set at creation

returns.claimAddress: The address recovered from the signature

refundFor(bytes32,uint256,address,addres.details: Permissionless: anyone may call once the timelock has passed, and the only      thing the caller decides is to pay the gas. The key names `sender`, and the      coins can only go there, so a wrong `sender` addresses a swap that does not      exist rather than redirecting one that does. A sender that cannot receive the      native coin is not reachable this way; it uses the destination variant itself.

params.claimAddress: Claim address that was set at creation
params.preimageHash: The preimage hash used at creation
params.sender: Sender (refund address) that was set at creation; receives the coins
params.timelock: Timelock that was set at creation

rehash(bytes32,uint256,uint256,bytes32,u.details: Collaborative rehash, consented to exactly like `refundBySig`: the sender by      being msg.sender, the claimAddress by an EIP-712 signature over the old terms      (with `sender = msg.sender`) and the new ones. Lets a swap whose far side      failed (an unpayable Lightning invoice, say) be retried under a fresh hash      without unwinding the lock. Nothing is paid out and `lockedTotal` does not      move: the old key becomes Rehashed and the new key Active, with the same      amount, sender and claimAddress.      The new timelock must lie in the future, as at creation, and must not be      shorter than the current one: a rehash never shortens the timelock, so the      claimAddress keeps at least the claim window it was promised, whatever it      signed. Equal or later is accepted.      No `SwapCreated` fires for the new key — consumers follow `SwapRehashed`.      The new key is taken on a first-come basis like any other: a third party who      learns the agreed terms can `create` under them first and make this call      revert with `SwapExists`. That costs them a lock the claimAddress may redeem      and leaves the original untouched, so the parties simply agree on fresh terms.

params.newPreimageHash: Preimage hash the lock continues under
params.preimageHash: The preimage hash used at creation
params.timelock: Timelock that was set at creation

returns.claimAddress: The address recovered from the signature
returns.newKey: The key the lock continues under

renounceOwnership().details: Disabled: recovery is owner-gated, so an ownerless contract could never release      a mis-sent balance again. Use `transferOwnership` / `acceptOwnership` instead.

params.key: The swap key (see `computeKey`, or the `key` field of `SwapCreated`)

transferOwnership(address).details: Starts the ownership transfer of the contract to a new account. Replaces the pending transfer if there is one. Can only be called by the current owner. Setting `newOwner` to the zero address is allowed; this can be used to cancel an initiated ownership transfer.

computeKey(bytes32,uint256,address,addre.notice: Compute the storage key for a swap from its parameters

create(bytes32,address,address,uint256).notice: Lock `msg.value` of the native coin with an explicit refund address

create(bytes32,address,uint256).notice: Lock `msg.value` of the native coin into a new hash time-locked swap

isActive(bytes32,uint256,address,address.notice: Check whether a swap with the given parameters is active

recoverExcess(address).notice: Recover the balance held beyond what active swaps are owed

recoverToken(address,address).notice: Recover ERC20 tokens sent to this contract by mistake

redeem(bytes32,uint256,address,uint256).notice: Redeem the coins by revealing the correct preimage (direct claim)

redeemBySig(bytes32,uint256,address,uint.notice: Redeem the coins using an EIP-712 signature from the claimAddress (gasless / delegated)

refund(bytes32,uint256,address,uint256).notice: Reclaim the coins after the timelock has expired

refund(bytes32,uint256,address,uint256,a.notice: Reclaim the coins after the timelock has expired, sending to a specified destination

refundBySig(bytes32,uint256,uint256,uint.notice: Refund before the timelock: the sender calls, the claimAddress signs

refundFor(bytes32,uint256,address,addres.notice: Refund an expired swap on the sender's behalf; the coins go to the sender

rehash(bytes32,uint256,uint256,bytes32,u.notice: Replace the hash lock and timelock of an active swap, keeping the coins locked

swapState(bytes32).notice: A swap's lifecycle state and (if redeemed) its revealed preimage,         by swap key — one read classifies a settled swap without log scans
